editorial:
Ever felt like your morning commute was a total disaster? You will definitely relate to the struggle in this new film. After making a hit about lost buses, Gio Petti turns his camera toward the chaotic world of Ottawa's rail system. You get to follow Petti as he digs into the messy expansion of Line 2. It is not just about trains and tracks, though. You will meet real people who rely on these trains to get to work and school, all while local politicians turn the whole project into a huge shouting match. The vibe is a mix of frustration and hope, making you feel like you are riding right there with the commuters.

What really works here is how the film stays grounded. The pacing is quick, and the interviews feel like honest conversations rather than stiff reports. While some of the political talk can get a bit dry, the human stories keep you hooked. You should definitely check this out if you love stories about city life or just want to see someone fight for a better system.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with a hopeful look at the future. After showing all the failures and delays, the final scenes show a group of citizens starting their own movement to hold the city accountable. There is no magic fix for the trains, but the twist is that the power shifts from the politicians to the riders. It ends with a shot of the first successful test run, proving that change is actually possible.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves city stories or hates bad public transit.
